metadata.title: The Influence of Folk Art on Contemporary Artistic and Design Practices
metadata.description:
Abstract: This study aims to examine the influence of folk art and crafts on modern design practices. It will focus on how designers can find innovative ways to apply folk art aesthetic, design languages to evolve and integrate new design languages. The second aspect is how designers can take advantage of technology to achieve desired effects without disturbing the traditional values of the folk arts and crafts. Folk art is deeply rooted in the cultural essence of a region, profoundly influenced by its soil, nature, and geographical characteristics. The close connection between people and their environment is evident in their artistic expressions, where bold and straightforward forms reflect their intrinsic bond with nature. This connection is further exemplified in their vibrant use of colors, linear depictions, and decorative motifs that breathe life into their homes, attire, and everyday objects. The graphic qualities of folk art—its simplicity, charm, and directness—remain fascinating and captivating.
India boasts a rich and diverse tradition of folk art and craft. Each region’s artistic expressions mirror the country’s cultural diversity, shaped by the distinct geographical features of its provinces. Folk art and craft are inseparable from the daily lives of the people, intricately linked to their festivals, rituals, and seasonal changes, which are often tied to agricultural and religious practices. These art forms embody the rhythm of life, weaving together nature and human activity.
For artists and designers, this vibrant lifestyle and its associated art forms—such as dance, music, textiles, pottery, cane work, and geometric crafts—offer a wealth of inspiration. These folk traditions present unique opportunities for exploring functionality, aesthetics, and decoration. The simplification of forms and motifs, particularly of animals, birds, and flora, often serves as a creative foundation for modern interpretations.
This study delves into the inspirational impact of folk art on contemporary artists and illustrators, many of whom have formal training in modern or academic art. Despite their backgrounds, these creators often integrate elements of tribal and folk art into their work, blending these influences with their unique design sensibilities to produce innovative artistic expressions. By analyzing these works, this study uncovers how folk-art traditions resonate within modern creative practices and explores the artistic parameters that define this interaction.
In addition to artistic creations, designers and illustrators have found innovative ways to apply folk aesthetics in communication design. The influence of folk art is evident in advertising, publication design, environmental graphics, outdoor publicity, and editorial illustrations. These contemporary applications demonstrate the enduring relevance of folk aesthetics, as they resonate strongly with the cultural psyche, creating a sense of “Indian-ness” that connects with people across social strata and popular culture. The impact of folk art extends beyond individual creations, influencing the broader field of design education. By studying how artists and designers adapt folk aesthetics, we can identify key inspirational elements that inform modern teaching methodologies.
Practical Implications: Practical exercises based on these findings can be integrated into contemporary design education, fostering a deeper appreciation of folk traditions while equipping students with innovative tools for creative expression. The approach of this study encourages the continuation of folk art’s legacy, ensuring its relevance in modern artistic and design practices. The study not only highlights the cultural significance of these traditions but also offers a roadmap for their integration into the evolving landscape of art and design.

metadata.title: eDemOS: a Shiny application bundle for online participation and deliberation
metadata.description: Companion software for the AMULET eDemOS deliberative platform. The bundle comprises a hub (amulet-main), a card-sorting questionnaire on open science (amulet-cards) with a results dashboard (amulet-cards-results), a proposal-voting module (amulet-decidim), a Pol.is-style deliberation module (amulet-delib), and a shared data/helpers module (amulet-global). Public demo: no login, no data is saved. Developed within project AMULET CZ.02.01.01/00/22_008/0004558.

metadata.title: Structural Mechanisms of Collision Dependence in Constructibility Jacobians
metadata.description:
For polynomial observables of a fixed resonance-free discrete dynamical system, we ask when
a coefficient map’s generic Jacobian rank can be certified independently of any particular pa-
rameter value. We prove that a family is immune to special-parameter rank deficiency whenever
it admits a full-rank Jacobian minor built entirely from collision-free coefficients, and we identify
two distinct mechanisms by which this immunity can fail. The first is dimensional: when the
minimal coefficient count equals the state dimension, the Jacobian has a unique minor, forcing
collision dependence whenever any coefficient is collision-dependent. The second is algebraic:
even when several candidate collision-free minors exist, they may be constrained to an alge-
braic variety of positive codimension, forcing rank deficiency independently of dimension count.
We establish this second mechanism via a discriminant-type identity among coefficients and a
general chain-rule bound, and verify both mechanisms against every family examined in a com-
panion paper, yielding a complete structural classification. Two simple explanatory hypotheses
considered in that companion paper – that collision count, or the number of shared algebraic fac-
tors, alone determines rank behaviour – are shown to be insufficient; For the analysed families,
structural forcing is the only criterion found to separate every family correctly.

data.title: Structural Mechanisms of Collision Dependence in Constructibility Jacobians

metadata.title: CONSTITUTIONAL INTERPRETATION: THE CONSTITUTIONAL COURT'S PARADIGM SHIFT IN THE JUDICIAL REVIEW OF PRESIDENTIAL AND VICE-PRESIDENTIAL CANDIDACY THRESHOLD NORMS IN INDONESIA
metadata.description: The presidential threshold provision under Article 222 of Law No. 7 of 2017 on General Elections has generated prolonged debate concerning the inclusivity of electoral competition and the integrity of the presidential system. For over a decade, the Constitutional Court consistently upheld this norm as an open legal policy of the legislature. However, a fundamental shift occurred through Decision No. 62/PUU-XXII/2024, which declared the provision unconstitutional. This study analyzes the structure of the Constitutional Court's legal arguments in its prior jurisprudence and examines the legal rationale underlying the paradigm shift in this recent decision. This is a normative legal study employing statutory, case, and conceptual approaches. The findings indicate that the earlier jurisprudence relied on judicial restraint to maintain government stability and promote the simplification of the political party system. In contrast, Decision No. 62/PUU-XXII/2024 applies the doctrine of responsive judicial review, emphasizing substantive justice, the restoration of popular sovereignty, equality among political parties participating in the current general election, and the determination of the framers' original intent. The invalidation of this norm creates a technical legal vacuum, requiring the legislature to restructure the regulatory framework through new constitutional engineering for the 2029 General Election. This restructuring must combine the guarantee of inclusive rights—free from percentage thresholds—with a mandatory nomination mechanism to preserve stable and democratic electoral management.
keywords: Threshold; Open Legal Policy; Constitutional Court; Constitutional Interpretation; Constitutional Engineering.

metadata.title: PCC-Explorer
metadata.description:
PCC-Explorer is an open-source software tool to assess the impact of GNSS antenna Phase Center Corrections (PCC) on geodetic parameters.

PCC-Explorer allows researchers and practitioners to analyze how PCC differences propagate into estimated geodetic parameters
such as coordinates and tropospheric delays.

metadata.title: ULTR-AI: Ultrasound-led TB Recognition Using AI
metadata.description: ULTR-AI is research software for developing and evaluating artificial intelligence models that analyze lung ultrasound for pulmonary tuberculosis triage. The codebase supports direct image-to-TB prediction, prediction of human-recognizable lung ultrasound signs, patient-level aggregation, and evaluation against study outcome labels.

metadata.title: Snapquery: FAIR Management of Query Sets to Mitigate Query Rot in Knowledge Graphs
metadata.description:
Will the “cats” Wikidata SPARQL query example still work in the future? While link rot has been a known issue, the Query Rot problem has not been investigated much in the past. We introduce an approach for quality assessment and refactoring of query sets and evalu- ate its implementation for SPARQL.

By applying information hiding and dependency inversion principles, we hide the details of the query and introduce the snapquery SPARQL query endpoint middleware to maintain expected query behavior independently of technical details, context, and even, as a future option, the query lan- guage. “snapquery cats” is designed to work consistently in the future no matter what changes. This approach enables the swapping of endpoints, conceals the complexity of (federated) queries, and manages SPARQL query sets by making the queries FAIR first-class citizens of the Knowl- edge Graph infrastructure. The increased abstraction aligns well with state-of-the-art Artificial Intelligence approaches that allow the use of natural language input to generate query sets.

This novel, systematic, and semi-automatic approach is generally useful in most knowledge graph management scenarios. It allows for the gath- ering of query metadata from real-world environments on the fly, sup- porting the creation of test suites, benchmarks, challenges, dashboards, and other analytical applications for query performance and health moni- toring. Our approach contributes to advancing knowledge engineering by bridging gaps between knowledge graphs, software engineering, and large language models.

We reproduce use cases of the Scholia, QLever and general Wikidata projects to demonstrate functionality and measure non-functional quality improvements over those projects.
We conclude that advancing Knowledge Graph management requires 1. introducing queries as FAIR first-class citizens by developing platform- independent named parameterized queries (thus confirming a 2019 pro- posal), 2. structured, implementation-independent error messages, and 3. shifting to higher abstraction levels that support human and machine generated general text input. We suggest corresponding improvements to the SPARQL standard.

metadata.title: IN VIVO EVALUATION OF THE WOUND-HEALING POTENTIAL OF NANOZINC GEL CONTAINING ZINC OXIDE NANOPARTICLES
metadata.description: The development of topical formulations containing zinc oxide nanoparticles has attracted considerable attention because of their antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, and regenerative properties. The present study aimed to evaluate the wound-healing efficacy of NanoZinc gel in an in vivo excisional wound model. The study was performed using fifteen healthy white mice randomly divided into control and treatment groups. Full-thickness excisional skin wounds (1 cm in diameter) were created under aseptic conditions. Animals in the treatment group received topical NanoZinc gel (0.02%, 2 mg/kg), whereas the control group was treated with sunflower oil. Wound healing was monitored for 14 days by measuring wound area using ImageJ software. Statistical analysis was performed using one-way ANOVA with GraphPad Prism 8.0 (p < 0.05). NanoZinc gel significantly accelerated wound contraction compared with the control group. Faster epithelialization and granulation tissue formation were observed from day 5 onward, with almost complete wound closure by day 9. No signs of skin irritation or local toxicity were detected. The obtained findings indicate that NanoZinc gel possesses pronounced wound-healing activity and represents a promising topical formulation for further preclinical and clinical investigations

metadata.title: Radiological Outcomes Following Total Hip Replacement: A Prospective Evaluation of Implant Stability and Osteointegration
metadata.description:
Background: Total hip replacement (THR) is a highly successful reconstructive procedure for the management of end-stage hip disorders. While clinical outcomes following THR are well documented, radiological assessment remains essential for evaluating implant positioning, osteointegration, component stability, and early postoperative complications. However, data regarding radiological outcomes following THR in rural and tribal populations of central India remain limited.

Objective: To evaluate the radiological outcomes, implant stability, and osteointegration following total hip replacement through serial postoperative radiographic assessment.

Methods: A prospective observational study was conducted in the Department of Orthopaedics, Raipur Institute of Medical Sciences, Raipur, Chhattisgarh, India, over a period of 18 months. Seventy-nine patients undergoing primary THR for end-stage hip pathology were included. Standardized anteroposterior radiographs of the pelvis and operated hip were obtained preoperatively, immediately postoperatively, at 3 months, and at 6 months. Acetabular component assessment was performed using the DeLee and Charnley classification, while femoral component evaluation was based on the Gruen zonal system. Radiographs were analyzed for implant stability, osteointegration, radiolucent lines, component migration, loosening, and osteolysis.

Results: A total of 79 patients were included in the study, with a mean age of 44.16 ± 13.85 years; 61 (77.2%) were males and 18 (22.8%) were females. Serial radiographic evaluation demonstrated satisfactory implant positioning and stability in the majority of patients throughout the follow-up period. Radiolucent lines were observed in DeLee and Charnley Zone III in 5 patients (6.3%) and in Gruen Zone IV in 6 patients (7.5%). No radiolucencies were detected in DeLee and Charnley Zones I and II. There were no cases of component migration, stem subsidence, acetabular or femoral component loosening, or osteolysis during the six-month follow-up period. Stable implant fixation was observed in 74 patients (93.7%), and radiographic findings were consistent with satisfactory osteointegration and biological fixation.

Conclusion: Total hip replacement demonstrated excellent short-term radiological outcomes, with favorable implant positioning, successful osteointegration, and a high rate of implant stability. The limited radiolucencies observed were not associated with implant failure or clinical instability. These findings support the effectiveness of THR in achieving reliable early radiological outcomes in patients from rural and tribal populations and highlight the value of serial radiographic assessment in postoperative surveillance.
